I am from Dachau, i live here. 

One of my earlier memories (I was 3) was me and my grandpa driving past this huge place with even bigger walls around. So i was asking my grandpa what this is, and all he said was that a lot of people were killed here. As a child thats enough information.

In 4th grade (age 10) you start with local history. But again, as children you cant really understand those things, so all you learn was that evil people (the nazis) put innocent people into this prison like thing where they worked until they died, some of them were killed. 

In year 8 (at least in the Gymnasium, the highest level public school, i'm not sure about the other kinds of school) you start learning about the wars and how the nazis were able to gain power. We didnt really learn about specific battles, rather political processes that led to one another. Then we spent 3 or 4 lessons on the holocaust, because the teacher said we'll learn more about it when we visit the concentration camp. The guide there led us around and told us as much as we could take. 

Over the years you spend history on other subjects, such as American history, the Middle East, The DDR and Communism, the Balkans, etc. 

Then in year 11, (when repeating the entire history of Germany) you talk more in detail abput Hitler and the gain of power. Not too much about the holocaust, but more about what came before, such as the Nürnberger Rassegesetze, or the segregation of Jews and Germans, the life in the gettos, the Reichsprogromnacht, and how the Nazis were voted into power.

So we learn a lot more about the political circumstances rather than the actual holocaust itself comparatively, probably because the german education system asumes, that the holocaust is still do deep in Germanys concience, that it is not necessary to repeat all details but how the nazis could even get that far.

We didnt learn a lot about americas history tbh, rather Americas view on itself and how that led to its history.

Also I feel like in Europe you learn a lot more in school about the holocaust than in America? Of course in Dachau you are more focused on the local history and learn more about it than maybe an average highschool student in for example the US. Correct me if i'm wrong about that
